svg.title: Who attacks a cloud account, and how Falcon catches each one
svg.desc: Four scenarios play in turn. An external attacker with a phished login grants roles/owner to a Gmail account and Falcon raises gcp-privileged-role-granted. A malicious insider makes the customer exports bucket public: gcp-bucket-made-public. A CI pipeline hijacked by a poisoned dependency adds an exclusion to the audit log sink to hide itself: gcp-audit-logging-tampered. A careless engineer opens SSH to 0.0.0.0/0: gcp-firewall-open-to-internet. Each time the audit event flows through Pub/Sub, normalize and detect to Slack and BigQuery.
svg.text: Who attacks a cloud account, and how Falcon catches each one

svg.text: Inside Falcon, a few seconds later
None of them uses malware. They call ordinary Google APIs, and every call lands in Cloud Audit Logs, which is exactly what Falcon reads.
